Claim 1 (Currently amended): A method for preparing a cryopreserved acellular dermal matrix comprising: i) removing the epidermis from allograft skin that has not been transplanted onto an organism; ii) removing cells from the dermis of the allograft skin; iii) mixing glycerol and a basic solution selected from a buffer solution and an animal cell culture medium; iv) dissolving sucrose in the basic solution to a final concentration of 20 to 40% by weight to obtain a cryoprotectant; v) penetrating the cryoprotectant into the allograft skin from which the epidermis and cells in the dermis are removed; vi) freezing the cryoprotectant-penetrated allograft skin in a controlled rate freezer; and vii) recovering the cryopreserved acellular dermal matrix.

Claim 2 (Currently amended): The method for preparing a cryopreserved acellular dermal matrix according to claim 1, wherein the mixing ratio of glycerol and the basic solution is 0.5-3:9 based on weight.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The method for preparing a cryopreserved acellular dermal matrix according to claim 1, wherein the final concentration of sucrose is 30% by weight in the basic solution.

Claim 8 (Currently amended): An autograft substitute comprising the cryopreserved acellular dermal matrix which is prepared by the method according to any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the cryopreserved acellular dermal matrix is characterized by the absence of viable cells and the presence of a cryoprotectant.
